subject.title: Gmail hook delivery verification fails even when message tool uses Telegram target

question: For hook runs with no resolved delivery target, should a successful explicit `message` tool send to a concrete Telegram target complete delivery verification, while preserving strict matching when the mapping did specify a target?
rationale: The source path and user-visible failure are clear, but accepting a direct send as delivery changes the contract that controls retries and fallback behavior for targetless hook mappings.

options.title: Accept explicit direct sends
options.body: Recommended: treat a successful channel-and-target `message` send as verified only when the hook has no planned target, and retain planned-target comparison when one exists.

options.title: Require configured destinations
options.body: Keep targetless direct sends unverified and require hook mappings to carry a resolved delivery target before a direct tool send can complete delivery.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit direct sends
recommendation.body: Recommended: treat a successful channel-and-target `message` send as verified only when the hook has no planned target, and retain planned-target comparison when one exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent direct-send and delivery-target work makes this the closest available historical routing candidate.
